chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Nabīdh has touched my garment; may I perform salat in it? He said: Yes. I said to him: A drop of nabīdh fell into a jar from which I drink? He said: Yes. Indeed, the basis of nabīdh is halal, while the basis of khamr is haram.

key_terms.أُصَلِّي: I perform salat, referring to the validity of prayer in the garment
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine or intoxicating drink whose basis is forbidden
key_terms.ثَوْبِي: my garment, the clothing in which salat is performed
key_terms.حُبٍّ: a large jar or vessel from which one drinks
key_terms.قَطْرَةٌ: a drop, indicating a very small amount
key_terms.نَبِيذٌ: a fermented drink referred to here as having a basis of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Can one pray in a garment touched by nabīdh, and what is the ruling if a drop of it falls into a drinking vessel?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling regarding nabīdh and distinguishes it from khamr. It indicates that contact with nabīdh does not prevent salat in a garment, and that a small amount falling into a vessel does not render it forbidden, because the original ruling of nabīdh is halal whereas the original ruling of khamr is haram.
